There's no information in the article to understand what the problem is.

It sounds like a number of mods are being copied without permission from the PC version and upoaded on the XB1 version:

It was the second most popular mod for Xbox One, and DogtoothCG said he plans to release the next version of the mod to both PC and the console. However, “constant trawling of the web for unauthorized uploads” of the mod is taking up a lot of his time.

The footnoted PC Gamer article is more clearly written:

  • 'Stolen' Fallout 4 mods appear on Xbox :: PCGamer :: Archive

Ordinarily VG24/7 has good content, but I agree that the author kind of mangled this one.

Once GTAV came out on pc and I moved last my consoles haven't come put of their boxes. So I'm not entirely sure what's going on in the console world, both those articles are the types that I've written to the authors and made complaints about.

If consoles are being opened up by the developers to allow mods like they're PC's I don't really see what the problem is.

If they're adding mods to the games as updates and claiming that it's their content then yeah that's a problem.

I think it's only a problem if they're stealing content, allowing a console to run like a steam machine isn't an issue.

It sounds like the situation is as follows: Bethesda has allowed mod integration in Fallout 4 on PC for a while now, and just recently updated the Xbox One with this integration as well. It sounds like porting existing Fallout 4 (PC) mods to the Xbox version isn't difficult, but it isn't done automatically, so mod creators have to port their mods over to the XB1 to make them available on that platform.

But some other third parties are beating mod creators to the punch and are porting their mods over and claiming them as their own content. I don't think anyone has a problem with the system Bethesda's implemented or hold Bethesda responsible for the theft, just that the "mod gold rush" has sparked some interesting news as third parties steal mods from the PC version of Fallout before their actual creators can move them over to the Xbox One.
